newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan govt says to cut drug prices by 3% in April.
newsitem.headline: Japan govt says to cut drug prices by 3% in April.

text.p: The Japanese government will cut drug prices under the National Health Insurance system by an average of three percent in April, an official of the Ministry of Health and Welfare said on Friday.

The government has reviewed the pricing system under which it reimburses hospitals for the drugs they dispense in conjunction with a rise in Japan's sales tax by two percentage points to five percent in April, the official said.
Although a tax increase usually means an increase in drug prices, a decline in market prices from official rates has allowed the government to cut prices instead, he said.
He also said prices of 7,718 drugs out of the total of 11,974 items listed in the government health insurance system would be cut.

"The price cut's impact on the drug industry will be very large, considering that drug prices were cut by an average of 6.8 percent only a year ago," said Takeshi Bito, managing director of the Japan Pharmaceutical Manufacturers Association.
He said drug makers would be forced to review their marketing strategies now hospitals are likely to demand a reduction in makers' prices.

Pharmaceutical companies usually sell drugs at prices lower than official rates, allowing hospitals to profit from the difference. If the companies decide to maintain their prices, they may face a decline in orders.
A Reuters poll on Friday showed that Japanese pharmaceutical makers plan to cut their drug prices by an average of three percent following the official drug price cut.
The following are the companies' planned average price reductions:
Sankyo Co Ltd -2.4 percent
Takeda Chemical Industries Ltd around -2.5 percent
Yamanouchi Pharmaceutical Co Ltd -3.0 percent
Daiichi Pharmaceutical Co Ltd none available
Shionogi & Co Ltd about -1.5 percent
Tanabe Seiyaku Co Ltd none available
Fujisawa Pharmaceutical Corp around -3.0 percent
Banyu Pharmaceutical Co Ltd -0.1 percent
Chugai Pharmaceutical Co Ltd -3.3 percent
Eisai Co Ltd -4.5 percent
Ono Pharmaceutical Co Ltd none available
A spokesman for Banyu said that there was no special reason why the firm planned to cut prices at a rate lower than the poll average.
Eisai, which plans to cut prices by an average of 4.5 percent, the highest among the firms polled, said the cut would not have a significant impact on the company's earnings.
